ratings_why.fun: The curve has a shape I want: Age grows by a set amount each turn, but Novice, Painter and the Eldest pay per Age, so stats grow faster and faster, with Awaken 20 as a late chase; the cost is a thin board in rounds 3-6.
ratings_why.distinct: Age you can move, plus oldest/youngest targeting, gives fresh routing play, but the core still reads close to Hedgerow folk's turns-in-slot clocks.

verdict_why: The growth shape is right; one rules gap on Lamplighter Hrošč is worth closing before it settles.

points.text: Say whether two Lamplighter Hrošč stack (x4) or not. With a golden one beside it, that decides whether the Robber-Knight and Dragon of the Springs run at x3 or x6.
If the golden ceiling runs too hot, let golden Brother Netopir copy Age once a turn and move it as normal after that. That keeps the high roll worth chasing and stops it compounding.
The Long Sleep has no decision after turn 6. One card that lets you spend a lot of Age at once for a spike (for example in the Pressure-Sense Olm style) would give the patient line a timing call.

Beehive Painter is the tribe's best curve piece. A second card that reads oldest and youngest the other way round, feeding the oldest by the youngest's Age, would reward keeping one newcomer on purpose.

standouts.why: Its growth follows the oldest unit's Age, so it climbs every turn, and it feeds a carry from another tribe: a great Tier 4 job.
Brother Netopir turns board geometry into an Age relay, and every play beside him is a real decision.
The Eldest grows the whole board faster as it ages, and Awaken 20 gives the late game a doubling to chase.

weakest.why: On a full Olm board almost everything already has Still, so Cloister Warden is a 3/4 that only matters in the half-Olm build.
Parkelj the Dark does little on a board that sits still, which is weak for a Tier 5 direction card.

flags.note: Golden Netopir plus golden Echo Bat: copy onto a bought unit, sell it, and twice that Age lands on your youngest. Rotated well, Age roughly triples per buy-sell cycle, limited only by gold.
Age has no cap and opponents can't touch it, so with Hrošč the Robber-Knight wipes the enemy board at Start of Combat once your units reach about Age 10.
The text doesn't say whether a second copy stacks.
